[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard defines the mandatory requirements for deploying and operating containerized workloads at Gainwell Technologies using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) Auto Mode. It establishes EKS Auto Mode as the sole approved container compute platform for all new containerized workloads, and defines enforceable requirements for cluster provisioning, workload configuration, security posture, observability, and operational governance.
page_texts.6:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#scope]

### Scope

**In scope**: All new containerized workloads deployed to Kubernetes (EKS) in AWS after the effective date. This includes net-new application deployments, platform services, and workloads migrated from other compute models as part of modernization programs.

**Out of scope**: Existing containerized workloads operating on non-EKS compute prior to the effective date (subject to a separate migration standard). Container images deployed to AWS Lambda are not governed by this standard — Lambda provides its own execution environment and does not use Kubernetes primitives (pods, namespaces, network policies). Non-containerized workloads on EC2 are not governed by this standard. Application-layer concerns (language runtimes, frameworks, test tooling) are governed by application-domain standards.

> **Clarification — Lambda container images vs. EKS containers**: AWS Lambda supports deploying functions as container images. These workloads run in the Lambda execution environment, not on Kubernetes. This standard applies exclusively to workloads orchestrated by EKS (deployed as Kubernetes pods). Teams choosing Lambda as their compute model — whether using ZIP packages or container images — are outside the scope of this standard. However, teams deploying long-running services, multi-container workloads, or workloads requiring Kubernetes-native capabilities (service discovery, rolling deployments, persistent storage) **must** use EKS Auto Mode per this standard and **must not** use Lambda as a substitute for container orchestration.
page_texts.7:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory.** All teams deploying new containerized workloads in AWS **must** comply with every requirement in this standard. Non-compliance requires a formal Architecture Exception approved by the Architecture Review Board (ARB) through the Change Review Board (CRB) process.
page_texts.8:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Gainwell Technologies' modernization strategy (ADR-IFR-004) establishes containers as the target compute model. Without an enterprise-wide standard defining how containers are deployed and operated, teams independently select infrastructure configurations, producing inconsistent security postures, uncontrolled cost exposure, operational fragmentation, and gaps in HIPAA-required controls.

EKS Auto Mode eliminates undifferentiated operational overhead by managing node provisioning, scaling, and lifecycle through Karpenter and AWS-managed node classes. Standardizing on this model ensures:

- Uniform security baseline (Pod Security Standards, network policy, secrets management) across all containerized workloads
- Consistent operational model enabling Platform Gainwell to provide shared infrastructure services
- Auditable provisioning through infrastructure-as-code pipelines, satisfying HIPAA change-control requirements
- Reduced time-to-production for delivery teams through pre-approved, governed infrastructure patterns

[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-001-eks-auto-mode-as-mandatory-compute-platform]

#### REQ-EKS-001: EKS Auto Mode as Mandatory Compute Platform

All new containerized workloads **must** be deployed to Amazon EKS clusters configured in Auto Mode.

- **REQ-EKS-001a**: Self-managed node groups and managed node groups **must not** be created outside of EKS Auto Mode managed node classes. Manual node group provisioning bypasses Karpenter-managed scaling and lifecycle and is **prohibited**.
- **REQ-EKS-001b**: AWS Fargate profiles **must not** be used as a substitute for EKS Auto Mode. Fargate may only be used where explicitly approved as a standalone exception.
- **REQ-EKS-001c**: ECS (Elastic Container Service) **must not** be used for new containerized workloads after the effective date of this standard.

**Rationale**: EKS Auto Mode consolidates node provisioning, scaling, and lifecycle management under a single AWS-managed control plane, eliminating per-team node management overhead and providing a uniform operational target for Platform Gainwell services.
page_texts.12:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-002-cluster-provisioning-via-infrastructure-as-code]

#### REQ-EKS-002: Cluster Provisioning via Infrastructure-as-Code

All EKS clusters **must** be provisioned through Platform Gainwell infrastructure-as-code (IaC) pipelines.

- **REQ-EKS-002a**: Clusters **must** be defined using approved Terraform modules and Terragrunt deployment configurations maintained by Platform Gainwell.
- **REQ-EKS-002b**: Manual cluster creation through the AWS Console, AWS CLI, or `eksctl` is **prohibited** for production and pre-production environments.
- **REQ-EKS-002c**: All cluster configuration changes **must** be applied through the IaC pipeline. Out-of-band changes that create configuration drift **must** be remediated within the same sprint in which they are detected.
- **REQ-EKS-002d**: Cluster Kubernetes version **must** be within two minor versions of the latest EKS-supported release. Clusters running an end-of-life Kubernetes version are non-compliant.

**Rationale**: IaC-provisioned clusters provide an auditable, repeatable, and reviewable record of infrastructure state, satisfying HIPAA change-control requirements and enabling consistent security baselines across environments.
page_texts.13:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-003-gitops-continuous-delivery-via-argo-cd]

#### REQ-EKS-003: GitOps Continuous Delivery via Argo CD

All application workloads deployed to EKS **must** use Argo CD for GitOps-based continuous delivery, as defined in GUID-INFRA-K8S-001.

- **REQ-EKS-003a**: Every workload **must** have a corresponding Argo CD Application or ApplicationSet resource managing its deployment lifecycle.
- **REQ-EKS-003b**: Direct `kubectl apply` commands applied to production clusters outside of Argo CD sync operations are **prohibited** except for declared break-glass procedures documented in the runbook.
- **REQ-EKS-003c**: Application manifests **must** be stored in version-controlled Git repositories and **must** not be generated or modified at deployment time outside of approved templating tools (Helm, Kustomize).

**Rationale**: GitOps delivery through Argo CD enforces the declarative cluster state, provides a continuous compliance verification mechanism, and creates an auditable deployment record required for change management and incident response.
page_texts.14:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-004-pod-resource-management]

#### REQ-EKS-004: Pod Resource Management

All pods deployed to EKS **must** declare resource requests. Resource limits **should** be set for memory.

- **REQ-EKS-004a**: Every container spec **must** include `resources.requests.cpu` and `resources.requests.memory`. Pods without resource requests **will be rejected** by admission policy.
- **REQ-EKS-004b**: `resources.limits.memory` **should** be set for all containers. Memory limits are strongly recommended to prevent unbounded memory consumption and OOMKill cascades.
- **REQ-EKS-004c**: CPU limits **should not** be set in most cases. CPU throttling caused by CPU limits is a known source of latency degradation in Kubernetes workloads. Teams **must** document their rationale when CPU limits are applied.
- **REQ-EKS-004d**: LimitRange resources **must** be defined in each namespace to enforce default resource constraints for containers that do not explicitly declare them.

**Rationale**: Resource requests are required for the Kubernetes scheduler to make correct placement decisions and for Karpenter to provision appropriately-sized nodes. Absent requests lead to node overcommitment, workload instability, and unpredictable cost.
page_texts.15:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-005-pod-security-standards--restricted-profile]

#### REQ-EKS-005: Pod Security Standards — Restricted Profile

All pods **must** comply with the Kubernetes Pod Security Standards (PSS) at the `restricted` profile level.

- **REQ-EKS-005a**: Namespaces **must** be labeled to enforce the `restricted` Pod Security Admission (PSA) policy. Labels **must** include `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted`.
- **REQ-EKS-005b**: Privileged containers (`securityContext.privileged: true`) are **prohibited** without a formal Architecture Exception granted by the ARB.
- **REQ-EKS-005c**: Containers **must** run as non-root (`runAsNonRoot: true`). Containers configured to run as UID 0 are **prohibited** without an Architecture Exception.
- **REQ-EKS-005d**: `hostNetwork`, `hostPID`, and `hostIPC` **must** be set to `false` for all pods. Access to host namespaces is **prohibited** without an Architecture Exception.
- **REQ-EKS-005e**: Containers **must** set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` and drop all Linux capabilities (`capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`). Only explicitly required capabilities **may** be re-added with documented justification.
- **REQ-EKS-005f**: Root filesystems **must** be set to read-only (`readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`) unless the container explicitly requires write access to the root filesystem, in which case writable paths **must** be mounted as `emptyDir` volumes.

**Rationale**: The `restricted` PSS profile enforces the principle of least privilege at the container level, reducing the blast radius of container escapes and mitigating privilege escalation attack paths. This is a baseline control for PHI-handling workloads.
page_texts.16:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-006-observability-via-opentelemetry]

#### REQ-EKS-006: Observability via OpenTelemetry

All workloads deployed to EKS **must** implement OpenTelemetry instrumentation as defined in STD-APP-MON-002.

- **REQ-EKS-006a**: Applications **must** emit distributed traces, structured metrics, and structured logs using OpenTelemetry SDKs or auto-instrumentation agents.
- **REQ-EKS-006b**: OpenTelemetry Collector **must** be deployed as a DaemonSet or sidecar as directed by the platform team, and **must** be configured to export telemetry to the enterprise-designated observability backend.
- **REQ-EKS-006c**: Health probes (`livenessProbe` and `readinessProbe`) **must** be defined for all containers. Startup probes **should** be defined for containers with long initialization times.

**Rationale**: Consistent observability telemetry is the operational foundation for incident detection, root cause analysis, and SLO tracking. Without mandatory instrumentation, PHI-related incidents may go undetected, violating HIPAA breach notification requirements.
page_texts.17:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-007-networking--vpc-cni-and-service-mesh]

#### REQ-EKS-007: Networking — VPC CNI and Service Mesh

Workloads **must** use the AWS VPC CNI for pod networking, as managed by EKS Auto Mode.

- **REQ-EKS-007a**: Alternative CNI plugins (Calico, Cilium, Weave) are **prohibited** unless an Architecture Exception is granted and a validated migration path from VPC CNI is documented.
- **REQ-EKS-007b**: Service mesh adoption is optional. When a service mesh is adopted, it **must** be AWS App Mesh or Istio. No other service mesh implementation is approved.
- **REQ-EKS-007c**: If mTLS is required between services, it **must** be implemented through the approved service mesh. Application-layer TLS without service mesh **should** be documented as a compensating control in the service's architecture record.
- **REQ-EKS-007d**: External load balancers provisioned for workloads **must** use the AWS Load Balancer Controller managed by Auto Mode. Directly managed `LoadBalancer` service types without the controller are **prohibited**.

**Rationale**: AWS VPC CNI assigns VPC-native IP addresses to pods, enabling AWS security groups at the pod level, simplifying network policy enforcement, and providing full network observability through VPC Flow Logs — a HIPAA-required control.
page_texts.18:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-008-storage--managed-csi-drivers-only]

#### REQ-EKS-008: Storage — Managed CSI Drivers Only

Stateful workloads requiring persistent storage **must** use AWS-managed CSI drivers provided through EKS Auto Mode.

- **REQ-EKS-008a**: Persistent storage **must** use the EBS CSI driver (for block storage) or the EFS CSI driver (for shared file storage). Both are managed by Auto Mode.
- **REQ-EKS-008b**: `hostPath` volumes **must not** be used for persistent data storage. `hostPath` usage is **prohibited** except for explicitly approved system-level integrations (e.g., container runtime socket mounts for monitoring agents) with a documented Architecture Exception.
- **REQ-EKS-008c**: Local ephemeral storage (`emptyDir`) **may** be used for temporary, non-persistent data only.
- **REQ-EKS-008d**: StorageClass resources **must** use the `WaitForFirstConsumer` volume binding mode to ensure volumes are provisioned in the same availability zone as the consuming pod.
- **REQ-EKS-008e**: PersistentVolumeClaims **must** set an appropriate `storageClassName`. The use of the default storage class without explicit declaration is **prohibited** for production workloads.

**Rationale**: Managed CSI drivers ensure EBS/EFS volumes are provisioned with encryption-at-rest (a HIPAA required control) and lifecycle management integrated with cluster node operations. `hostPath` volumes create persistent data tied to specific nodes, creating data loss risk and preventing workload mobility.
page_texts.19:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-009-secrets-management-via-external-secrets-operator]

#### REQ-EKS-009: Secrets Management via External Secrets Operator

Sensitive configuration values and credentials **must not** be stored as native Kubernetes Secrets without external secrets integration.

- **REQ-EKS-009a**: Secrets **must** be stored in AWS Secrets Manager or HashiCorp Vault as the authoritative source.
- **REQ-EKS-009b**: The External Secrets Operator (ESO) **must** be used to synchronize secrets from the external store into Kubernetes Secrets. Direct creation of Kubernetes Secrets containing sensitive values is **prohibited**.
- **REQ-EKS-009c**: Kubernetes Secrets created by ESO **must** have a defined `refreshInterval` aligned with the secret rotation policy of the application.
- **REQ-EKS-009d**: Secrets **must not** be committed to Git repositories or embedded in container images, ConfigMaps, or environment variable definitions in Helm values files or Kustomize overlays.
- **REQ-EKS-009e**: IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) **must** be used to grant ESO and application workloads access to AWS Secrets Manager. Static IAM credentials **must not** be used.

**Rationale**: Native Kubernetes Secrets are base64-encoded, not encrypted, in etcd by default. Centralizing secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or Vault with ESO synchronization ensures encryption-at-rest, access-auditing, and automated rotation — all required controls for PHI-handling applications under HIPAA.
page_texts.20:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-010-container-image-security]

#### REQ-EKS-010: Container Image Security

Container images **must** be sourced from approved ECR registries and **must** meet security baseline requirements before deployment.

- **REQ-EKS-010a**: Container images **must** be pulled from designated Gainwell ECR registries only. Images pulled from public registries (Docker Hub, quay.io, ghcr.io) directly into production or pre-production environments are **prohibited**.
- **REQ-EKS-010b**: All images **must** be scanned for vulnerabilities using ECR Enhanced Scanning (powered by Amazon Inspector) before deployment. Images with Critical or High severity CVEs **must not** be deployed without a documented risk acceptance approved by the Security team.
- **REQ-EKS-010c**: Base images **must** use Platform Gainwell approved golden images. Custom base images **must** be derived from approved golden images and published to the internal ECR registry.
- **REQ-EKS-010d**: Images **must not** be tagged with `latest` in production deployments. All production image references **must** use immutable digests (`image@sha256:...`) or explicitly pinned version tags.
- **REQ-EKS-010e**: An admission webhook (e.g., Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper policy) **must** be configured to enforce image source and signing requirements at admission time.

**Rationale**: Unvetted images from public registries are a primary attack vector for supply-chain compromise. ECR-centralized image management with vulnerability scanning enforces a consistent security baseline and provides an auditable provenance chain for deployed workloads.
page_texts.21:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-011-namespace-isolation-and-network-policy]

#### REQ-EKS-011: Namespace Isolation and Network Policy

Each application or service **must** have its own dedicated Kubernetes namespace. Network traffic between namespaces **must** be restricted by default.

- **REQ-EKS-011a**: Each application or independently deployed service **must** be assigned a dedicated namespace. Multi-tenant namespaces shared by unrelated applications are **prohibited**.
- **REQ-EKS-011b**: A default-deny NetworkPolicy **must** be applied in every application namespace, denying all ingress and egress traffic not explicitly permitted.
- **REQ-EKS-011c**: Cross-namespace traffic **must** be explicitly permitted through NetworkPolicy resources. Implicit cross-namespace communication is **prohibited**.
- **REQ-EKS-011d**: Namespace resource quotas **must** be defined to prevent any single workload from exhausting cluster-level resources.
- **REQ-EKS-011e**: Namespace naming **must** follow the enterprise naming convention: `{product}-{environment}` (e.g., `claims-processing-prod`, `provider-portal-staging`).

**Rationale**: Namespace-level isolation is the primary workload boundary in Kubernetes. Default-deny network policies limit the lateral movement radius if a workload is compromised, satisfying HIPAA's minimum-necessary access principle for inter-service communication.
page_texts.22:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#req-eks-012-workload-autoscaling]

#### REQ-EKS-012: Workload Autoscaling

All production workloads **must** define Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) configurations. Node scaling is managed automatically by Karpenter through EKS Auto Mode.

- **REQ-EKS-012a**: A HorizontalPodAutoscaler resource **must** be defined for every production Deployment and StatefulSet.
- **REQ-EKS-012b**: HPA **must** configure `minReplicas` to at least 2 for production workloads to ensure availability during pod disruptions.
- **REQ-EKS-012c**: HPA scaling metrics **must** be based on CPU utilization, memory utilization, or custom metrics aligned with application-specific load indicators. Scaling configurations not validated against load test results are non-compliant for production deployments.
- **REQ-EKS-012d**: PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) resources **must** be defined for all production Deployments and StatefulSets to protect availability during node drain operations.
- **REQ-EKS-012e**: Teams **must not** manually configure Karpenter NodePools or EC2NodeClasses. Node provisioning configuration is managed exclusively by Platform Gainwell through IaC pipelines.

**Rationale**: HPA ensures workloads scale with demand, preventing both over-provisioning cost and under-provisioning outages. Karpenter-managed node scaling through Auto Mode eliminates the operational burden of node lifecycle management while providing cost-optimized, just-in-time provisioning.

page_texts.23:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- **Service mesh for inter-service mTLS**: Teams handling PHI in inter-service communication **should** adopt the approved service mesh (App Mesh or Istio) to enforce mTLS, even when not explicitly required by the security tier classification.
- **Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA) in recommendation mode**: Teams **should** deploy VPA in `Off` mode (recommendation only) alongside HPA to collect resource utilization data and right-size resource requests over time.
- **CPU limits avoidance**: Teams **should** avoid setting CPU limits. If limits are set, teams **should** validate that the application does not exhibit CPU throttle-induced latency under normal operating load.
- **Ephemeral containers for debugging**: Teams **should** use `kubectl debug` with ephemeral containers for production debugging rather than running privileged debug pods.
- **Image distroless bases**: Teams **should** use distroless base images where the runtime supports it, minimizing the attack surface of deployed containers.
- **Namespace-level resource budgets**: Teams **should** define LimitRange and ResourceQuota objects in every namespace, not just those with known abuse risk.

---
page_texts.24:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

The following practices are **prohibited** for all EKS workloads governed by this standard:

| Prohibited Practice | Reason |
|---------------------|--------|
| Self-managed node groups (without Architecture Exception) | Bypasses Auto Mode lifecycle management and creates operational fragmentation |
| `kubectl apply` to production outside of Argo CD | Violates GitOps control model; creates unauditable state changes |
| Images pulled from public registries directly | Supply-chain risk; bypasses vulnerability scanning and provenance controls |
| Privileged containers (`privileged: true`) | Violates Pod Security Standards; high blast radius on compromise |
| `hostPath` volumes for persistent data | Ties data to a single node; blocks workload mobility and node replacement |
| Native Kubernetes Secrets with sensitive values without ESO | etcd not encrypted at rest by default; violates secrets management policy |
| Container images tagged `latest` in production | Non-deterministic deployments; prevents reproducible rollback |
| Hardcoded credentials in ConfigMaps, Helm values, or image layers | Credential exposure risk; violates secrets management policy |
| Manual Karpenter NodePool/EC2NodeClass configuration | Creates provisioning drift outside IaC control |
| CPU limits on latency-sensitive workloads without validation | CPU throttling causes latency degradation without resource exhaustion |

---

[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

Teams that cannot comply with a requirement in this standard due to a legitimate technical, operational, or regulatory constraint **must** follow the formal Architecture Exception process.

1. **Identify the specific requirement**: Reference the requirement ID (e.g., REQ-EKS-001a) in the exception request.
2. **Document the constraint**: Describe the technical, operational, or regulatory reason compliance is not achievable.
3. **Assess the risk**: Identify the security or operational risks introduced by the exception, with a proposed compensating control for each risk.
4. **Submit to CRB**: Submit the Architecture Exception request through the Change Review Board (CRB) process with ARB sign-off required.
5. **Define expiry**: All exceptions **must** include an expiry date (maximum 12 months). Permanent exceptions require annual re-approval.
6. **Document the exception**: Approved exceptions **must** be recorded in the application's architecture record and referenced in the IaC configuration comments.

Known pre-approved exception categories (still require CRB documentation):

| Scenario | Permitted Deviation | Pre-approved Compensating Control |
|----------|--------------------|------------------------------------|
| DaemonSet workloads requiring privileged access (e.g., node-level monitoring agents) | Self-managed node group for DaemonSet pods only | Restrict to non-production environments; production requires full ARB review |
| Security tooling requiring `hostPID` or `hostNetwork` access | `hostPID`/`hostNetwork` on designated security tooling pods | Restrict to dedicated `platform-security` namespace; enforce RBAC limiting pod creation |

---
page_texts.28:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#eks-auto-mode-cluster-baseline]

#### EKS Auto Mode Cluster Baseline

| Parameter | Required Value | Notes |
|-----------|---------------|-------|
| Cluster mode | Auto Mode enabled | EKS Auto Mode must be active at cluster creation; cannot be retrofitted |
| Kubernetes version | Within 2 minor versions of latest EKS release | Checked quarterly by Platform Gainwell |
| Cluster endpoint access | Private endpoint enabled | Public endpoint **should** be disabled for production clusters |
| Secrets encryption | AWS KMS key (customer-managed) | Required for HIPAA encryption-at-rest for etcd secrets |
| Control plane logging | API, audit, authenticator, controller manager, scheduler | All control plane log types **must** be enabled and directed to CloudWatch Logs |
| VPC configuration | Private subnets in at least 2 AZs | Multi-AZ required for production; single-AZ permissible for development |
page_texts.29:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#node-class-configuration]

#### Node Class Configuration

Node class configuration is managed exclusively by Platform Gainwell through IaC. Teams **must not** create or modify `EC2NodeClass` or `NodePool` resources. Platform Gainwell provides:

| Node Class | Instance Family | Use Case |
|------------|----------------|----------|
| `general-purpose` | `m7i`, `m7g` | Standard application workloads |
| `compute-optimized` | `c7i`, `c7g` | CPU-intensive processing workloads |
| `memory-optimized` | `r7i`, `r7g` | Memory-intensive workloads (caches, data processing) |
| `gpu` | `g5`, `p4d` | ML inference workloads (requires separate approval) |

Teams specify node class affinity through `nodeSelector` or `nodeAffinity` using the label `gainwell.io/node-class: <class-name>`.
page_texts.31:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#required-pod-spec-fields]

#### Required Pod Spec Fields

All pod specifications **must** include the following fields. The admission webhook will reject pods missing required fields.

```yaml
spec:
  containers:
    - name: my-container
      image: <ecr-registry>/<image>@sha256:<digest>
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: "250m"        # Required — must reflect measured baseline utilization
          memory: "256Mi"    # Required — must reflect measured baseline utilization
        limits:
          memory: "512Mi"    # Recommended — set to 2x request as starting point
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000      # Must be non-zero
        allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
        capabilities:
          drop: ["ALL"]
  securityContext:
    seccompProfile:
      type: RuntimeDefault
```
page_texts.32:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#limitrange--namespace-default]

#### LimitRange — Namespace Default

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: default-limits
  namespace: <app-namespace>
spec:
  limits:
    - type: Container
      default:
        cpu: "500m"
        memory: "256Mi"
      defaultRequest:
        cpu: "100m"
        memory: "128Mi"
      max:
        cpu: "4"
        memory: "4Gi"
```
page_texts.34:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#external-secrets-operator--externalsecret-resource]

#### External Secrets Operator — ExternalSecret Resource

```yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: my-app-secrets
  namespace: <app-namespace>
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    name: aws-secrets-manager
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
```

[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#phase-1-platform-prerequisites-platform-gainwell-responsibility]

#### Phase 1: Platform Prerequisites (Platform Gainwell Responsibility)

Before teams can onboard, Platform Gainwell **must** establish:

1. Provision EKS Auto Mode clusters per environment (development, staging, production) using the approved Terraform modules.
2. Deploy and configure Argo CD with the enterprise GitOps configuration (per GUID-INFRA-K8S-001).
3. Deploy and configure External Secrets Operator with ClusterSecretStore resources pointing to AWS Secrets Manager.
4. Configure Pod Security Admission (PSA) enforcement at the `restricted` level across all namespaces.
5. Deploy admission webhooks (Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper) for image policy, resource request, and security context enforcement.
6. Configure ECR Enhanced Scanning (Amazon Inspector) and integrate scan results into the deployment pipeline gate.
7. Publish approved golden base images to internal ECR registries.
8. Configure cluster-level observability: OpenTelemetry Collector DaemonSet, CloudWatch Container Insights.
page_texts.45:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#phase-2-application-team-onboarding]

#### Phase 2: Application Team Onboarding

1. Request namespace provisioning through the Platform Gainwell self-service portal, following the naming convention `{product}-{environment}`.
2. Configure an Argo CD Application resource in the team's GitOps repository.
3. Create ExternalSecret resources for all application secrets, replacing direct Kubernetes Secret definitions.
4. Update container image references to use the internal ECR registry with pinned digest tags.
5. Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation per STD-APP-MON-002.
6. Define HPA, PDB, LimitRange, ResourceQuota, and NetworkPolicy resources.
7. Validate pod specs pass the PSA `restricted` policy using `kubectl apply --dry-run=server`.
page_texts.46:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#phase-3-production-readiness-validation]

#### Phase 3: Production Readiness Validation

Before promoting to production, teams **must** complete:

1. Run vulnerability scan on all container images and confirm no Critical/High CVEs without approved risk acceptance.
2. Validate HPA scales correctly under synthetic load using the approved load testing tool.
3. Confirm Argo CD sync status is `Healthy` and `Synced` with no outstanding drift.
4. Confirm all health probes are configured and responding correctly.
5. Verify network policies permit required traffic paths and block all others.
6. Confirm observability telemetry is flowing to the enterprise backend (traces, metrics, logs).

[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Requirement | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
|-------------|----------|--------------------|--------------------|
| REQ-EKS-001 | Cluster has Auto Mode enabled | `aws eks describe-cluster` — verify `computeConfig.enabled: true` | Terraform plan output |
| REQ-EKS-002 | Cluster provisioned via IaC | No manual cluster creation events in CloudTrail | CloudTrail audit log |
| REQ-EKS-003 | Workload managed by Argo CD | Argo CD Application exists and reports Synced | Argo CD UI / `argocd app list` |
| REQ-EKS-004 | Resource requests defined | `kubectl describe pod` shows non-zero requests | Admission webhook rejection log |
| REQ-EKS-005 | PSA restricted enforced | `kubectl get ns --show-labels` shows `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted` | Namespace label output |
| REQ-EKS-006 | OTel instrumentation active | Traces visible in observability backend for all request paths | Trace sampling report |
| REQ-EKS-007 | VPC CNI in use | `kubectl get daemonset -n kube-system aws-node` reports desired pods ready | DaemonSet status |
| REQ-EKS-008 | CSI storage only | No `hostPath` volumes in any production pod spec | Kyverno policy audit report |
| REQ-EKS-009 | ESO-managed secrets | No manually created Kubernetes Secrets with secret data | ExternalSecret inventory scan |
| REQ-EKS-010 | ECR images with digest | Pod image references contain `@sha256:` | Kyverno policy audit report |
| REQ-EKS-011 | Default-deny NetworkPolicy | `kubectl get networkpolicy` shows `default-deny-all` in namespace | NetworkPolicy inventory |
| REQ-EKS-012 | HPA and PDB defined | `kubectl get hpa,pdb` lists resources for each production Deployment | Resource inventory scan |
page_texts.48:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#testing-requirements]

### Testing Requirements

- **Admission policy testing**: Run `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` against all manifests before committing to the GitOps repository. Pipeline gates **must** fail the build if any admission violations are detected.
- **Network policy validation**: Use `netshoot` or equivalent tooling to validate that intended paths are open and unintended paths are blocked before production promotion.
- **Scaling validation**: Execute load tests against staging environments to confirm HPA scaling behavior before production deployment. Validate that Karpenter provisions new nodes within the target SLA (typically <90 seconds from pod pending state).
- **Secrets rotation testing**: Validate that ESO refreshes secrets without application restart on each secret rotation. Rotation tests **must** be executed in staging before enabling rotation in production.
- **Vulnerability scan gate**: CI/CD pipeline **must** gate on ECR scan results. Pipelines that deploy images with unresolved Critical or High CVEs without approved risk acceptance are non-compliant.

#### Assessment Criteria

| Area | Criterion | Assessment Frequency |
|------|-----------|---------------------|
| Cluster configuration | EKS Auto Mode enabled; Kubernetes version within supported range | Quarterly automated scan |
| IaC compliance | No CloudTrail events indicating manual cluster or node group creation | Continuous — CloudTrail anomaly detection |
| GitOps compliance | All workloads have Argo CD Application; no out-of-band `kubectl apply` events | Weekly Argo CD drift report |
| Security posture | All namespaces enforce PSA `restricted`; no privileged pods without approved exception | Weekly Kyverno policy audit |
| Secrets management | No manually created Kubernetes Secrets with secret data; all secrets sourced from ESO | Weekly secret inventory scan |
| Image compliance | All production images in ECR with digest references; no Critical/High CVEs without risk acceptance | Per-deployment CI gate + weekly scan |
| Resource requests | No pods missing CPU/memory requests | Admission webhook (real-time) |
| Observability | All workloads emit traces, metrics, and logs to enterprise backend | Monthly observability coverage report |
page_texts.52:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#assessment-process]

#### Assessment Process

1. **Automated scanning**: Platform Gainwell runs weekly automated compliance scans across all EKS clusters using Kyverno policy reports and custom AWS Config rules.
2. **Compliance dashboard**: Findings are surfaced in the Platform Gainwell compliance dashboard, visible to application teams and the EA practice.
3. **Remediation SLA**: Critical findings (privileged containers, public image pulls, missing secrets management) **must** be remediated within 5 business days. High findings within 15 business days. Medium findings within the next sprint.
4. **Reporting**: Quarterly compliance summary reports are provided to the Architecture Review Board.
page_texts.53:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#monitoring-requirements]

### Monitoring Requirements

- **Continuous monitoring**: Kyverno policy reports provide real-time admission violation tracking. AWS Config rules detect cluster configuration drift.
- **Periodic reviews**: Platform Gainwell conducts a quarterly review of this standard against the current EKS Auto Mode feature set and Kubernetes release cadence.
- **Incident reporting**: Compliance incidents (e.g., privileged pod deployed without exception, public image pull detected in production) **must** be reported to the Platform Gainwell security team within 24 hours of detection.
- **KPIs**: The following metrics are tracked quarterly:
  - Percentage of workloads fully compliant with this standard
  - Number of open Architecture Exceptions and average exception age
  - Mean time to remediate compliance findings by severity
page_texts.55:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#exception-categories]

#### Exception Categories

- **Temporary exceptions**: Valid for up to 12 months. Require a documented remediation plan with milestone dates.
- **Permanent exceptions**: No permanent exceptions are pre-approved under this standard. Long-running deviations require annual ARB re-approval.
- **Emergency exceptions**: Break-glass deviations for production incidents may be authorized by the on-call Platform Gainwell engineer. An Architecture Exception request **must** be filed retrospectively within 5 business days.
page_texts.56:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#exception-management-process]

#### Exception Management Process

1. Author an Architecture Exception document referencing the specific requirement ID.
2. Document the technical, operational, or regulatory constraint preventing compliance.
3. Define compensating controls for each risk introduced.
4. Submit to CRB with ARB sign-off required.
5. Record approved exception in the application's architecture record with expiry date.
6. Platform Gainwell tags the workload in the compliance dashboard as `exception-approved`.

[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#example-1-onboarding-a-new-stateless-api-service]

#### Example 1: Onboarding a New Stateless API Service

**Context**: A new REST API service (`claims-adjudication-api`) is being deployed to the `claims-adjudication-prod` namespace.

**Implementation**:

- Namespace `claims-adjudication-prod` is provisioned via Platform Gainwell self-service portal with PSA `restricted` label, default-deny NetworkPolicy, LimitRange, and ResourceQuota applied automatically.
- Application Helm chart is updated to include resource requests, non-root security context, readOnlyRootFilesystem, dropped capabilities, and health probes.
- Secrets sourced from AWS Secrets Manager via ExternalSecret resources.
- Argo CD ApplicationSet references the Helm chart from the team's GitOps repo.
- HPA configured for CPU 70% target, minReplicas 2, maxReplicas 15.
- PDB configured with `minAvailable: 1`.
- NetworkPolicy permits ingress from the API gateway namespace only.
- ECR image reference uses `@sha256:` digest pinning.

**Compliance Evidence**: Argo CD sync status Healthy; Kyverno policy report zero violations; ECR scan shows no unresolved Critical/High CVEs; OTel traces visible in observability backend.
page_texts.61:
[standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md#example-2-requesting-an-exception-for-a-daemonset-monitoring-agent]

#### Example 2: Requesting an Exception for a DaemonSet Monitoring Agent

**Context**: The platform team deploys a node-level monitoring agent that requires `hostPID: true` and `hostNetwork: true` to collect node metrics.

**Implementation**:

- Architecture Exception filed referencing REQ-EKS-005d.
- Technical constraint documented: node-level metrics collection requires access to host PID namespace; no equivalent data is available through the Kubelet API or VPC Flow Logs alone.
- Compensating controls: agent pod restricted to `platform-monitoring` namespace; RBAC limits who can create pods in that namespace; image sourced from internal ECR with enhanced scanning; pod spec reviewed and approved by Security Engineering.
- Exception approved by ARB with 12-month expiry.
- Platform Gainwell tags the DaemonSet in the compliance dashboard as `exception-approved`.
